canonical_statement: The study aimed to estimate the causal effect of preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use on postoperative acute kidney injury in adults with type 2 diabetes undergoing emergency and non-emergency, cardiac and non-cardiac surgery.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we aimed to conduct a causal inference study using routinely collected data to emulate a target trial to examine the causal effect of preoperative SGLT2i use on the risk of postoperative AKI

canonical_statement: The investigators used routinely collected single-centre observational data to emulate a target trial, with surgery as time zero and follow-up through 7 postoperative days or discharge, whichever occurred first.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This was a causal inference study using routinely collected observational data designed to emulate a target trial

canonical_statement: Eligible patients were adults with type 2 diabetes taking glucose-lowering medication, admitted for at least 24 hours, undergoing surgery under general anaesthesia, with a baseline creatinine within 365 days before surgery and at least one creatinine within 7 days afterward.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We included adult patients (≥18 years of age) with type 2 diabetes who were admitted to hospital for at least 24 h

inclusion_criteria: Baseline creatinine within 365 days before surgery
At least one creatinine within 7 days after surgery

canonical_statement: Exclusions included type 1 diabetes, diet-controlled type 2 diabetes, non-surgical interventional procedures, missing required covariate data, preoperative AKI, and violations of the positivity or propensity-score overlap assumptions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with type 1 diabetes, diet-controlled type 2 diabetes, or who did not have diabetes were excluded.

canonical_statement: The exposure was documented preadmission use of an SGLT2 inhibitor before surgery; available agents were empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and ertugliflozin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The SGLT2i available in Australia at the time of the study were empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and ertugliflozin.

canonical_statement: The comparator group comprised surgical patients with type 2 diabetes who were not taking an SGLT2 inhibitor preoperatively.

canonical_statement: The primary outcome was postoperative AKI within 7 days, defined by KDIGO serum-creatinine criteria as an increase of at least 26.5 μmol/L over 48 hours or more than 1.5 times baseline within 7 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary outcome was postoperative AKI, defined as an increase in serum creatinine within 7 days postoperatively of ≥26.5 μmol/L over 48 h or >1.5 times baseline in 7 days

outcome.definition: Increase in serum creatinine within 7 days postoperatively of ≥26.5 μmol/L over 48 h or >1.5 times baseline in 7 days, per KDIGO consensus criteria.

canonical_statement: A directed acyclic graph identified covariates for the direct-effect analysis: age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index excluding age and sex, systolic blood pressure, baseline creatinine, baseline HbA1c, preadmission renin-angiotensin system inhibitor use, insulin use, surgical specialty, surgery duration, and emergency status.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The covariates used in our analysis were: age, sex, Charlson Comorbidity Index (excluding age and sex), systolic blood pressure, baseline creatinine, baseline HbA1c

canonical_statement: The primary causal contrast was the average treatment effect on the treated, estimated with propensity-score inverse probability of treatment weighting; standardized differences below 0.10 were treated as evidence of covariate balance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We estimated the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT), using inverse-probability of treatment weighting, based on the propensity score.

canonical_statement: Sensitivity analyses substituted baseline CKD for creatinine and excluded patients with baseline eGFR below 15 mL/min/1.73 m²; subgroup analyses examined emergency and non-emergency surgery.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We performed a sensitivity analysis by adjusting for the presence of baseline chronic kidney disease rather than baseline creatinine.

canonical_statement: Negative controls used preoperative DPP-4 inhibitor use as a negative-control exposure and thrombocytosis (>400 × 10^9/L) as a negative-control outcome.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To assess for residual bias, we utilised dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4i) as a negative control exposure.

The authors concluded that preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with reduced odds of postoperative AKI in patients with type 2 diabetes undergoing surgery and that larger randomized studies are warranted.

canonical_statement: Residual unmeasured confounding remains possible despite target-trial emulation, covariate adjustment, sensitivity analyses, and negative controls.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Despite utilising a target trial emulation framework and adjusting for confounders, the potential for unmeasured confounding exists.

canonical_statement: Postoperative creatinine measurement was not standardized, and inclusion required at least one postoperative creatinine within 7 days, creating potential ascertainment and selection concerns.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The number and timing of postoperative creatinine checks was not standardised given the retrospective nature of the analysis.

canonical_statement: The study was conducted at a single tertiary centre, so transportability to other centres and health systems is uncertain.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This was a single centre study at a tertiary referral hospital, thus results may not be generalisable to all centres.

canonical_statement: The investigators could not determine when SGLT2 inhibitors were started or the exact duration for which they were withheld before surgery.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We were unable to ascertain when SGLT2i were commenced or how long SGLT2i were withheld preoperatively for.

canonical_statement: The cohort was limited to patients with type 2 diabetes receiving glucose-lowering medications, so findings do not apply to all surgical populations or all people with diabetes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We only included patients with type 2 diabetes who were taking glucose-lowering medications, and our results cannot be generalised to all patient groups.
